target_customer: Developers building Kinect motion-control apps and games, especially in Unity and in the browser
problem: Getting a Kinect sensor working with a development environment took installing several separate components. Zigfu bundled the drivers and middleware and offered Unity and browser plugins to get to a working motion app in minutes.
business_model: developer tools and middleware (pricing not found)

founders.name: Amir Hirsch
founders.background_notes: Named in VentureBeat (2011-08-24) as co-founder and listed on the YC page. No education or employers in an opened source.

founders.name: Ted Blackman
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page only.

founders.name: Roee Shenberg
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page only.

founders.name: Shlomo Zippel
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page only.

competitors.name: Microsoft Kinect for Windows SDK
competitors.what: Official Windows-only SDK for Kinect, an alternative to the OpenNI based stack Zigfu packaged (Zigfu also supported it)

technical_complexity.rationale: Packaging OpenNI, NITE and sensor drivers into one installer, plus Unity and browser plugins across Mac and PC, is integration work; the hard computer vision was done by PrimeSense and Microsoft.

defensibility.rationale: A layer over third-party middleware; Microsoft's SDK and OpenNI could add the same convenience, and the sensor platform was controlled by others.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Microsoft shipped an official SDK and later discontinued Kinect production (reported 2017), removing the platform. A 2013 mailing list post by the Zigfu developer said it was just him left and still in development.

market_need_then: Kinect was a new 2010 sensor with strong hobbyist and developer interest, and VentureBeat (2011-08-24) described Zigfu as getting from zero to working motion apps in minutes. No revenue data found.

branding.domain_note: The YC page lists breaks.nu as the website, not zigfu.com. The site returned HTTP 503 when fetched.
branding.community_and_virality: Developer community tutorials and a Unity Kinect mailing list thread discuss the Zigfu package (2012); no merch.

brand_strength.rationale: Known mostly inside the Kinect developer community; a trademark ZIGFU exists under Motion Arcade Inc. per Justia, but no brand press was found.

outcome_analysis: Zigfu bundled Kinect middleware and shipped Unity and browser plugins in the summer of 2011. A 2013 developer post says it was down to one person, and the YC page lists it as inactive, but no shutdown notice or post-mortem was found, so the cause is not public and no failure factor is assigned. Microsoft ending Kinect production later is context, not a sourced cause.
notes: Both rounds rest on single databases that disagree: CB Insights gives 20K (YC and Romulus Capital, 2011-06-27) and Bouncewatch gives 130K across three rounds with a seed on 2011-08-02. They may overlap, so totals are unverified. Competitors: only one rival is dated near the batch; OpenNI based tooling is what Zigfu packaged rather than a company. The status of the company after 2013 is unknown.
